George's Black Dog Swim

On Monday 30th Decemeber 16 year old George is embarking on a New Zealand first. He is swimming the return length of Queen Charlotte Sound to raise awareness and funds for I AM HOPE.

I AM HOPE is a youth and community focused support group run by The Key to Life Charitable Trust, started by Mike King, and for the last three years has been promoting positive attitudinal societal change in schools and communities up and down the country, and funding private care and counselling for young people stuck-in-the-mud on waiting lists.

Follow George's Black Dog Swim progress from the 30th Dec to the 8th January live here - http://ow.ly/bd4630q2uRL 

If you would like to contribute to Black Dog Swim with a donation and inspirational message of support the Black Dog Swim givealittle page is: https://givealittle.co.nz/fundraiser/black-dog-swim-for-nz-youth-mental-health

Muslim Migrant Experiences - Event at Ngā Puna Waiora Newtown Library

In February we hosted a special launch event for international migration magazine NANSEN's latest issue, focused on Muslim migrants in Aotearoa and what “home” means to them. We were joined by journalist Muzhgan Samarqandi and editor Ronia Ibrahim, along with publisher and editor Vanessa Ellingham, who discussed their heartfelt stories shared in the magazine.

If you weren't able to join us at Ngā Puna Waiora Newtown Library please enjoy this video recording of this wonderful discussion. We'd like to extend our appreciation and thanks to Muzhgan, Ronia and Vanessa for joining us for this fabulous event!

You can also reserve a copy of Issue 03 of NANSEN Magazine in our catalogue at wcl.govt.nz

National Pacific Disability Action Plan Survey

We are inviting Pacific disabled people and their aiga to share their experience of disability via an online survey. The survey, with alternate formats available, complements a series of talanoa being held across the country. The information gathered during the talanoa and through the survey will help us develop the National Pacific Disability Action Plan.

The survey will be available online until 12 May: https://bit.ly/49Nz9hI
If you would prefer to respond to the survey by sending a video, audio message, or via email, you can send it to pacificpeoples@whaikaha.govt.nz
For alternate formats of the survey, visit our website: https://bit.ly/3Ut0AZs

Video description: Tofa, a Pacific woman is wearing a blue and black patterned dress with a red necklace and red flower in her hair. Slightly behind her on the right is an NZSL interpreter. They are standing in front of a grey background.
